headline: CEO at Anchor Group | NetSuite Consulting + Development
companyName: Anchor Group NetSuite Consultants and Developers
position: Anchor Group NetSuite Consultants and Developers
about:
I lead Anchor Group, a company of ~45 Midwest-based NetSuite consultants and developers. 

We work as profit-generation partners, not just as a mindless dev shop. We care about the success of your business outcomes, not just whatever the original project requirements said.

We understand that our clients "don't know what they don't know" about NetSuite. They don't want to have to come up with ALL the solutions themselves. 

Our ideal clients want someone to provide them with recommendations of best practices rooted in what other businesses in their industry are doing. They want someone who pushes back on ideas and provides creative alternatives. 

They want a consultant who actually CONSULTS. Who works hard to build a relationship of earned, mutual trust. That kind of trust doesn't come for free.

Let's face it - NetSuite is big and complex. It would be crazy not to ask for help. 

No single one of my NetSuite consultants tries to do his job alone; they are constantly leaning on each other's expertise to get results quickly. It helps to reduce missteps and stupid mistakes (although we've made our share of those, too - that's part of the definition of an expert). 

Plus, it's more fun to work together than struggle alone. Our consultants have been invited to employee-only Christmas parties by our clients - they just wanted to hang out with us more!

experiences.description:
Grew our ERP consulting team by 4X.  Built training and apprenticeship program to ramp up new consultants and give them the support needed to reliably delivery high quality service.

Led net-new NetSuite ERP implementations and provided techno-functional solution design for several teams of consultants and developers.

One evening I wrote the code for our most popular bundle: "Find SuiteCommerce Associated Image", which at last count has been installed in over 30 NetSuite instances.

experiences.companyName: Anchor Group NetSuite Consultants and Developers
experiences.description:
Project managed SuiteCommerce website implementations as well as built automations and custom software within NetSuite for B2C retail, B2B wholesale distributors, manufacturers, home service companies, and a large accounting firm.

We needed a lead magnet and I knew a little bit about SuiteCommerce, so I wrote the first ever book to be published on NetSuite Ecommerce.

It's a blast to teach Latin as an active, living language!  Although providing immersion in the language is the most important thing, I also borrow pedagogical techniques from WAYK, Rassias, and the comprehensible input crowd.

I designed and taught courses on the philosophy of friendship, a rare and precious thing for today's college students.  We memorized poetry, read Aristotle, and discussed the cookie scene from Frog and Toad.

My first official academic teaching job.  I learned a lot about the meta-skills of teaching college, like pairing and squaring, how to design effective homework, how not to assign tests that take forever to grade...

I led two- and three- week leadership training wilderness expeditions in Wyoming, Utah, and Colorado.  I learned a lot about logistics, contingency plans, making risk assessments with real, scary consequences on the line, and communicating in stressful emergency situations.

I also prepared the next generation of rock climbing instructors in the program.  This forced me to learn how to explicitly identify, systematize in a repeatable way, and then teach the best practices I had learned intuitively and through experience.

I co-led novice backpackers on three week expeditions in Wyoming's Wind River Range.  Everyone lived.

Additionally, these were leadership training courses, so I coached my students in real-life applications of leadership.  This required prudently allowing my students to fail and then carefully turning those failures into learnings. Lessons about communicating clearly or being aware of the emotional state of your team tend to hit a lot harder when the consequences are starkly real: because you did X, everyone is now cold, wet, and hungry.  It's a much more efficient learning environment than theoretical classroom discussions.
My first government job.  I filed speeches, reorganized all the files in the office in a standard way, and wrote research reports.  Yep, definitely an internship.
My second (and last) government job.  I mostly wrote answers to constituent emails.  I remember needing to bring a security pass anytime I went to the bathroom.
